title: Method overloading versus overriding
answer: Overloading uses the same method name with different parameter lists and is resolved at compile time; inheritance is not required. Overriding occurs when a subclass provides a compatible instance method for an inherited method and runtime dispatch can select the subclass implementation. An override keeps the parameter signature, uses a compatible covariant return type, cannot reduce visibility, and cannot override final, private, or static methods. AeroTopo demonstrates both patterns across `LanguageLab.join` and `Product.resolutionMetres()`.
